world.rationale: With superintelligence, AI itself drives the result: I put AI-caused doom at about 3.5%, well above the card's 1%, because expert and researcher surveys cluster between 3% and 10% and the card's gap between a 6.8% level-4 chance and a 1% doom chance looks too wide for a true loss of control. Without superintelligence, nuclear war and pandemics carry most of the small doom risk, while climate, energy and state breakdown drive a large but mostly recoverable level-3 risk; war and disease sit a little above their cards because they add every channel and the noSi case includes futures where a catastrophe stopped AI. I go below the energy card's 3.8% level-4 chance with superintelligence, because cheaper solar, storage and robots should ease energy shortages more than AI demand tightens them. Abundance for 90% of humanity needs Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia to rise fifty- to a hundredfold with broad sharing, so it is near zero without superintelligence and under one in ten even with it.

places.rationale: Rich, well governed, low inequality and energy-secure, so steady growth is the base case and broad sharing of AI gains is likelier here than almost anywhere. Aging and low fertility are the main drag without superintelligence.
Strong institutions and wealth, but heavy energy imports, aging and slow growth make stagnation a real possibility without superintelligence.
High debt, very low fertility, high water stress and three-quarters of energy imported weigh on growth and raise climate exposure compared with the rest of Europe.
Room to catch up and energy self-sufficiency favour improvement, but the war-level military spending and weaker governance raise the chance of decline or collapse.

Highest living standard, energy exporter and home of frontier AI, so abundance is likeliest here with superintelligence; high inequality, debt and interest burden and polarisation keep the bad tails non-trivial.
Middle-income with energy and food surpluses, so a quarter above today is likely, but high violence, inequality and interest burdens hold back reaching abundance for nine in ten.
Extreme water stress, rising heat, fragile states and dependence on oil and gas income that may shrink make this the riskiest middle-income region, though desalination and solar help.

Starting from a very low base makes a quarter above today the likely outcome, while abundance would need roughly a hundredfold rise; climate vulnerability, weak states and fast population growth make collapse more likely than elsewhere.
Strong growth momentum, led by India, makes improvement the base case, but humid heat, very high water stress and a nuclear rivalry keep collapse risk elevated.
Capable states, strong industry and AI capacity favour gains, but the world's lowest fertility, fast aging and the risk of a great-power war over Taiwan weigh on the outlook.
Growing manufacturing economies and relative peace favour steady improvement, with sea-level rise, storms and heat as the main climate threats.
Dominated by rich, resource-exporting Australia and New Zealand, which do well in most futures, while poorer Pacific islands and Papua New Guinea pull down the share reaching abundance.
